title: Coefficient Hom from a locally finite projective sheaf
statement: Let $A,B$ be finite commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital ring homomorphism, and $T$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work in ordinary unbounded small-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $L$ be an $A$-module sheaf trivialized on an etale cover by constant finite projective $A$-modules; finite projective means a direct summand of $A^r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Put $P=L[0]$. Suppose $N$ has bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval $[a,b]$, $a\le b$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Then $P$ and $Q=R\mathcal Hom_A(P,N)$ have bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, and the evaluation transpose $F_TQ\to R\mathcal Hom_B(F_TP,F_TN)$ is an isomorphism, where $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the arrow is exactly $\mathrm{evaluationComparison}$ [def-coef-internal-adjunction-comparison-maps]. No flatness of $\varphi$, Noetherian hypothesis, global rank bound or nonemptiness is assumed.

proof.text: Restrict to the etale cover in the hypothesis. Each constant finite projective module is a direct summand of a finite free module. Its sheaf and degree-zero complex are flat. Finiteness of the coefficient ring makes these local values finite sets; the one-stratum partition proves constructibility. Exact restriction and the tensor/pullback comparison give Tor amplitude [0,0].

source.place: Paragraph 3: internal Hom from a site-perfect complex is its finite-projective dual tensor the second argument; move coefficient change through internal Hom by its finite-projective model

proof.text: For a free constant first argument A^r in degree zero and a bounded-below representative P of N (available from its bounded cohomology), the bounded-free RHom calculation gives Hom(A^r[0],P)=P^r. For a projective summand apply the inclusion and retraction to this identification. Its Hom has the same finite Tor interval and bounded cohomology as N. On intersections of the trivializing cover with constructibility strata of N the Hom cohomology is a finite projective summand of a finite sum of constructible cohomology sheaves. These properties descend to T. Only a bounded-below model is used here, matching the bounded-free RHom theorem; no bounded flat resolution of N is required.

source.place: Paragraph 3: internal Hom from a site-perfect complex is its finite-projective dual tensor the second argument; move coefficient change through internal Hom by its finite-projective model

proof.text: To compute scalar extension, replace N by a K-flat model P with flat terms; scalar extension is P tensor_A B. Since the first complex is finite free in degree zero, the Hom is P^r even when P is unbounded. Change of rings preserves K-flatness. For A^r[0], evaluation is the sum of coordinate products, so its B-transpose sends f tensor b to the function x ↦ f(x) tensor b. Evaluation on the standard basis identifies this with the identity of (P tensor_A B)^r. Naturality with respect to the split inclusion and retraction proves invertibility for each finite projective summand, including rank zero.

source.place: Paragraph 3: internal Hom from a site-perfect complex is its finite-projective dual tensor the second argument; move coefficient change through internal Hom by its finite-projective model

proof.text: The restriction comparisons for tensor and Hom carry evaluation to evaluation, so injectivity of the tensor-Hom transpose identifies the local maps with restrictions of the specified global evaluationComparison. Its cone restricts to zero on every member of the cover. Every geometric point lifts to one of those members; exactness and geometric-stalk conservativity make each cohomology sheaf of the cone zero. The cone is zero, hence the specified arrow is an isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem locallyProjectiveCoefficientHom
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (L : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat A))
    (hL : ∃ d : Scheme.LocallyConstantDatum L, ∀ i : d.cover.I₀,
      ∃ P : ModuleCat A, Module.Finite A P ∧ Module.Projective A P ∧
        Nonempty (L.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i) ≅
          (constantSheaf (T.smallEtaleTopology.over (d.cover.etalePrecoverageToEtale i))
            (ModuleCat A)).obj P))
    (N : DerivedCategoryModule A T)
    (hN : DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible A T N ∧
      ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b N) :
    (DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible A T
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L) ∧
      ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L)) ∧
    (DerivedCategory.isBoundedConstructible A T
        (((derivedHom (ModuleCat A) T).obj
          (op ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L))).obj N) ∧
      ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn A T a b
        (((derivedHom (ModuleCat A) T).obj
          (op ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L))).obj N)) ∧
    IsIso (evaluationComparison φ T ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj L) N)
